name: Bill
sample_note: Bill has exactly one spoken line in the source (ch004-d0034). Every rule below is drawn from that line plus the way others talk to and about him (ch004-p24, p27, p29) and his silent jury-box business (ch011-p09, ch012-p05, p55). Rules that extend beyond the single line are tagged inferred:true.

register.level: the put-upon odd-job lad of the White Rabbit's household: humble, breathless, rustic working-class English
register.summary: A willing underling everything is 'put upon' (ch004-p25). His one speech comes in gasps: dash-broken clauses, a polite 'thank ye', country grammar (up I goes), homely similes from the nursery toy box and the fireworks night (Jack-in-the-box, sky-rocket). He cannot explain what happened to him. At the trial he is silent — his voice is the squeak of his slate-pencil. Per SUP-002 (amended BIB-0027) a photoreal CGI lizard.

examples.text: Well, I hardly know—No more, thank ye; I'm better now—but I'm a deal too flustered to tell you—all I know is, something comes at me like a Jack-in-the-box, and up I goes like a sky-rocket!

catchphrases.text: I hardly know … / all I know is …

sentence_style.length: one long, breathless run-on chopped by dashes into 3-9-word gasps (the single line is 42 words); new lines for Bill should stay in gasps of under ten words

patterns.rule: Breathless dash-broken clauses: starts, stops, restarts; the thought is never finished cleanly.

examples.text: Well, I hardly know—No more, thank ye; I'm better now—but I'm a deal too flustered to tell you—

patterns.rule: Country grammar and dialect forms: 'ye' for you, 'a deal' for a great deal, historic present with -s on the first person (something comes at me … up I goes).

examples.text: …something comes at me like a Jack-in-the-box, and up I goes like a sky-rocket!

patterns.rule: Humble deference and self-deprecation: disclaims knowledge (I hardly know), declines what he is offered politely (No more, thank ye), reassures (I'm better now).

examples.text: Well, I hardly know—No more, thank ye; I'm better now

patterns.rule: Explains the world through homely, concrete similes from toys and fireworks, never abstract words.

examples.text: like a Jack-in-the-box, … like a sky-rocket!

patterns.rule: In the trial (ch011-ch012) he does not speak at all: his presence is sound business (squeaking slate-pencil, writing with one finger, ink trickling down his face). If a screenplay gives him a word there, it must be a mumbled, one-to-three-word apology or 'Yes, sir' — never an opinion.
patterns.reason: The source gives him no trial line (ch011-p09, ch012-p05, ch012-p55); a minimal-deference rule keeps any added line consistent with his only speech.

examples.text: (narrative) One of the jurors had a pencil that squeaked… (it was Bill, the Lizard)
(narrative) he now hastily began again, using the ink, that was trickling down his face
…I'm a deal too flustered to tell you…

address.to_superiors_and_fellows: ye (thank ye); he is addressed as 'lad' and 'old fellow' by the others (ch004-p24, p27) and answers in kind, never commanding
address.to_alice: never addresses her (they never meet face to face)
address.reason: Only one line; the address set is taken from that line and from how the Rabbit's workmen speak to him in ch004-p24/p27.

forbidden_words.reason: a household odd-job lad; bookish words are the Dodo's and the Mouse's, never his

forbidden_words.regex: \b(I order|I command|off with|you must|I insist|I'll soon)\b
forbidden_words.reason: everything is 'put upon' Bill (ch004-p25); he never gives orders

drift.change: At the Rabbit's house: flustered, breathless, grateful speech after the chimney kick.
In the jury-box: speech drops to nothing; he is conveyed by the squeak of his pencil and his dazed, open-mouthed stare (ch012-p05). Any added line stays a mumbled monosyllable.
drift.reason: No trial dialogue in the source; the silence is itself the drift.

backtest_markers.regex: \b(ye|a deal|up I goes|I goes|I comes|I says|comes at me)\b
\b(I hardly know|all I know is|thank ye|I'm better now|flustered)\b

backtest.method: marker-claim back-test (shared yardstick with pb1 and 01-story/dialogue-rewrite): a spoken source line hits when it matches >=1 backtest_markers regex and no forbidden_words regex; verse excluded; full definition runs/p3-dialogue-style-pb2/result.json#backtest_method
backtest.small_sample_warning: only 1 spoken source line(s); the hit rate is not statistically meaningful - rules tagged inferred:true carry the card beyond the source
